summary: Lincoln County, MT: a station reported in 1930 atop a pine, a cabin of 1931 and an L-4 tower of 1934 later destroyed; a 2020 trip report finds the tower in shambles.

facts.design: Platform atop a 60-foot pine tree; earlier 50-foot pole L-4 tower built 1934
facts.status_note: The Fire Lookout Association lists the site as gone; a 2020 trip report describes the tower in shambles, with trees over the summit

access.note: Reached on foot by a trail from the Flower Creek trailhead, per a 2020 trip report; no official access notice read

visit.trail_note: About a mile of trail from the Flower Creek trailhead, faint near the top; the trip report says to expect no view from the summit

corrections.proposed: Platform atop a 60-foot pine tree; earlier 50-foot pole L-4 tower built 1934
corrections.why: The L-4 design and 15.2 m (50 ft) height in the record match the 1934 pole tower, which the source says was destroyed in the late 1940s; the platform the page describes sits atop a pine
A 2020 trip report describes the lookout tower in shambles with trees over the summit, so the site is not simply gone; the Association list still says gone, so a human should check

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Association list says gone and firelookout.com describes a present platform; the 2020 trip report found the tower in shambles. Treated as ruins, not standing; a current photo would settle it.

A September 1930 item describes a station finished in 1930; firelookout.com dates the frame cabin to 1931 and the platform to 1921 to 1931. The record's 1931 fits the cabin, and the station may predate it.
The 1930 item gives 88 feet for the station and firelookout.com gives a 60-foot pine for the platform. The record's 15.2 m (50 ft) matches the 1934 L-4 pole tower, not either pine structure.

notes_for_editor: The record's L-4 design and 15.2 m height describe the 1934 pole tower, not the platform (see corrections). Staffing rests on a 1930 Western News item as quoted by Rex's page; the original newspaper was not checked. The trip report is dated October 2020, so the current condition may have changed since. The L-4 loss is only dated 'late 1940s', so it has no event entry. firelookout.com credits photos to the Fire Lookout Museum and Rex Kamstra, but no image URL was in the cache, so none were added.
